expected_level_description: You can: - describe agile working and the roles in a multidisciplinary digital team

You can: - understand how to apply basic techniques for the analysis of research data and synthesis of findings - effectively involve your team in analysis and synthesis - present clear findings that colleagues can understand and use
You can: - demonstrate some awareness of the diversity of users of government services and the need to make government services usable and accessible for everyone
You can: - explain the importance of working to a user research plan and of following standards for user research
You can: - describe who your stakeholders are and the importance of managing relationships with them - explain what your stakeholders find important and why

You can: - plan and conduct a user research project, with support - understand when to use basic user research methods and how to apply them correctly - effectively involve your team in research activities
You can: - describe how government services and technology affect how people behave - explain how user-centred practices are used to build services that adapt to changing user behaviour and needs
You can: - describe the main parts of the health and care system and the services the organisation supports - explain why patient safety and confidentiality matter in your work

skill: Ethical research with patients and care staff
expected_level_description: You can: - plan research sessions that get informed consent and protect participants' wellbeing and privacy - adapt sessions for people who are unwell, distressed, or in vulnerable circumstances, and know when to stop - recognise and report safeguarding concerns that come up in research
You can: - apply data protection principles to your work - contribute to data protection impact assessments - handle information requests and records correctly
You can: - recognise and challenge behaviour that excludes others - consider different needs when you plan your work
